issues.description: The problem statement and UML require Farm.animals to be a List<Animal> implemented with an ArrayList and instruct students to initialize an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor. However, the provided solution implements the animals attribute as a Set<Animal> backed by a HashSet (with getter/setter using Set). This structural mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about the expected collection type and the required initialization (List/ArrayList vs Set/HashSet).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent: either (A) update the solution to use List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() (and adjust getter/setter signatures to List), matching the UML and problem text; or (B) if Set semantics are intended, update the problem statement/UML to specify Set<Animal> and remove the ArrayList instruction so all artifacts agree.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and instructions) explicitly describes Farm.animals as a List and instructs initializing it with an ArrayList, but the provided solution implements the animals collection as a Set (HashSet). This is a mismatch of the same conceptual entity (the collection holding animals) across artifacts and changes collection semantics (ordering, duplicates). Students following the instructions to use an ArrayList may be confused when the reference solution uses a different collection type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent: update the solution to use List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() (and adjust getter/setter signatures to List) to match the UML and instructions, or alternatively update the problem statement and template to accept Set/HashSet and note the semantic differences. The preferred fix is to change the solution to List/ArrayList to preserve the stated requirements.
